meta.audience: The remnant of the house of Israel who are spared
principles: A dying man speaking to descendants of his enemies
A short list of things to know
Two records that establish each other

world_behind.title: The chapter is ten verses
world_behind.text: It is Mormon's closing address in the book that carries his name.

world_behind.title: The audience is the survivors' descendants
world_behind.text: Verse 1 speaks to the remnant of this people who are spared. Mormon 6:15 has just reported that his own nation is gone except for twenty-four men, so the only audience left in the hemisphere is the one that destroyed it.

world_behind.title: He hedges his own delivery
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says "if it so be that God may give unto them my words". Moroni 1:4 puts the same conditional on the same audience sixty years later, and 3 Nephi 21:2 makes the arrival of these words the sign that the gathering has begun.

world_behind.title: Four verses begin the same way
world_behind.text: Verses 2, 3, 4, and 5 all open with "Know ye". Nothing else in the volume runs the formula four times in four consecutive verses, and the effect is a creed rather than a sermon: identity, repentance, weapons, and Christ, one to a verse.

world_behind.title: Weapons come third
world_behind.text: Verse 4 tells them to lay their weapons down and take them up no more save God command it. Alma 24:18 has an earlier Lamanite generation do exactly that and covenant to it, so the instruction has a precedent among the people it is addressed to.

world_behind.title: Two records are named
world_behind.text: Verse 8 gives this record and the one that shall come to the Gentiles from the Jews. 1 Nephi 13:38 to 41 describes the same two books coming together, and 2 Nephi 29:8 argues for why two are needed. Mormon is stating in a farewell what the first writer in the volume had seen in vision.

world_behind.title: The book ends with Amen
world_behind.text: Verse 10 closes Mormon's own writing; Mormon 8 and 9 are Moroni's.

words.text: Instruments of war. The record uses the word fifty-five times and the King James Bible twenty-one. Verse 4 tells this people to lay them down.
A wound that carries venom. Treated at Alma 22:14. It appears four times in the record, and the King James Bible twice, both in 1 Corinthians 15.
Success in a contest. The record uses the word twelve times and the King James Bible twelve. Verse 5 gives it to Christ over the grave.
A burial place, and death itself. Treated at Helaman 14:25. The word turns up nineteen times here, and the King James Bible sixty-eight. Verse 5 pairs it with the sting of death.
Free of blame. Treated at Mosiah 4:25. The record uses the word eight times and the King James Bible ten.
Without stopping. Its count is once, here, in this book, while the King James Bible not at all. Verse 7 attaches it to praises.
Companies of singers. The record uses the word twice, here and at Mosiah 2:28, and the King James Bible not at all. Both uses put them above.

phrases.term: If it so be that God may give unto them my words
phrases.text: The condition he writes under. He cannot deliver the letter himself.

phrases.term: Know ye that ye are of the house of Israel
phrases.text: The first thing on the list, and the shortest verse in the chapter. Identity comes before instruction.

phrases.term: Ye must lay down your weapons of war, and delight no more in the shedding of blood
phrases.text: The instruction from a man killed by their ancestors. Alma 24:17 had recorded a people who did exactly this.

phrases.term: Take them not again, save it be that God shall command you
phrases.text: The one exception, stated in the same breath as the command. He does not make it absolute.

phrases.term: In him is the sting of death swallowed up
phrases.text: 1 Corinthians 15:55 in different words. Verse 5 has already given the victory over the grave.

phrases.term: To sing ceaseless praises with the choirs above
phrases.text: The description of the kingdom. Mosiah 2:28 had used the same phrase of joining them.

phrases.term: Which are one God, in a state of happiness which hath no end
phrases.text: The end of the sentence about redemption. Happiness is the last noun.

phrases.term: Not only in this record but also in the record which shall come unto the Gentiles from the Jews
phrases.text: Two books named in one clause. Verse 8 traces the second one's route.

phrases.term: If ye believe that ye will believe this also
phrases.text: The logic of the two records. 1 Nephi 13:40 had said the later would establish the truth of the first.

phrases.term: Ye are numbered among the people of the first covenant
phrases.text: Their standing stated as fact. It does not depend on what they do next.

phrases.term: First with water, then with fire and with the Holy Ghost
phrases.text: The order given in his last sentence. He calls it following the example of the Savior.

verses.label: v. 2–3
verses.title: A formula, and the shortest sentence in the chapter
verses.text: "Know ye that ye" opens verses 2 through 5, and scripture has the phrase five times in all, four of them here. The first of the four is eight words long: "Know ye that ye are of the house of Israel." Before repentance, before Christ, before baptism, the thing Mormon puts first is who they are, and he spends the fewest words on it.

verses.label: v. 4
verses.title: The odd clause, and the exception written into it
verses.text: Between repentance and belief stands a demand that is not doctrinal at all: "ye must lay down your weapons of war, and delight no more in the shedding of blood." The phrase occurs once in scripture. Then the qualifier, "take them not again, save it be that God shall command you." The man who commanded the last Nephite army does not close the door he walked through; he leaves it latched to a condition.

verses.label: v. 5
verses.title: Knowing hands over to believing
verses.text: Know runs the length of the chapter, seven uses in ten verses. Believe does not appear until verse 5 and then holds the rest of it, six uses in the closing six verses. The address begins by telling the remnant what to know about themselves and ends by telling them what to believe about someone else.

verses.label: v. 8–9
verses.title: The book puts a different book ahead of itself
verses.text: The gospel will be set before them "not only in this record but also in the record which shall come unto the Gentiles from the Jews, which record shall come from the Gentiles unto you." Verse 9 then puts the two in order: "this is written for the intent that ye may believe that; and if ye believe that ye will believe this also." The book states its own purpose as pointing at a different book, and takes second place in its own sentence.

verses.label: v. 10
verses.title: The last words are a condition, not a warning
verses.text: The sequence is exact, "first with water, then with fire and with the Holy Ghost, following the example of our Savior," and the close is "if it so be that ye believe in Christ, and are baptized... it shall be well with you in the day of judgment." Mormon has spent six books recording what happens to a people who would not. He ends by describing what happens to the ones who do.

chapter.title: He writes to the descendants of the people who destroyed his
chapter.text: Verse 1 names the remnant who are spared. There is nothing bitter in the ten verses.

chapter.title: He admits he may not be heard
chapter.text: Verse 1 makes delivery conditional on God. The letter is sent without a courier.

chapter.title: Identity is the first instruction
chapter.text: Verse 2 tells them who they are before telling them what to do. Everything after rests on it.

chapter.title: The command about weapons carries an exception
chapter.text: Verse 4 allows taking them up at God's command. He does not overstate his own case.

chapter.title: The list is short and ordered
chapter.text: Repentance, weapons, knowledge of the fathers, belief in Christ. Four verses, four things.

chapter.title: Two records vouch for each other
chapter.text: Verse 9 makes belief in one the road to the other. The argument runs in both directions.

chapter.title: The reward is described as singing
chapter.text: Verse 7 gives ceaseless praises and choirs above. The kingdom is pictured as sound.

chapter.title: Mormon's own writing ends here
chapter.text: Verse 10 closes with Amen. What follows in Mormon 8 and 9 is his son's.

applications.title: Write to people who may never read it
applications.text: He addressed descendants centuries out, unsure the words would arrive. Some work is sent without a delivery guarantee.

applications.title: Start with who someone is
applications.text: He told them their identity before their duty. Instruction lands differently once that is settled.

applications.title: Put the weapons down
applications.text: The command comes from a man whose people died by them. Refusing to delight in harm is a decision made before the provocation.

applications.title: Learn what your fathers knew
applications.text: Among the things they must come to is the knowledge of their fathers. Recovering what an earlier generation understood is listed here as a step in the work, not as an interest.

applications.title: Describe the good outcome
applications.text: The verse spends its length on the destination: dwelling in the presence of God, singing praises, a happiness that has no end. A warning with no picture of the alternative leaves people nothing to move toward.

applications.title: Two records, and he sends them to both
applications.text: He sends them to the gospel set before them in this record and also in the one that comes to the Gentiles from the Jews. Nothing in the sentence asks them to choose between the two.

applications.title: Let two witnesses check each other
applications.text: He points to a second record that confirms this one. Believing one thing well opens the next.

applications.title: It ends on being numbered
applications.text: The last verse tells them they will know they are a remnant of Jacob, numbered among the people of the first covenant. The book closes this address on membership rather than on achievement.

questions.text: What am I writing that someone else must deliver?
Do I actually know whose I am?
What weapon am I still holding?
Which of these do I say I believe and act as though I do not?
What would ceaseless praise be like for me?
What have I believed that opened something else?
Where in the order of water and fire am I standing?
